metadata.title: BASIC Programming Language Family — Comprehensive Knowledge Graph
metadata.subject: History, standards, syntax, dialects, implementations, platforms, education, applications, and related technologies
source_basis: User-provided BASIC reference text (article excerpt showing last edit 2026-09-06)
Curated technical and historical connections added for graph completeness
metadata.relationship_direction: Every relationship is directed from source to target; descriptions explain the direction and meaning.

identifier_conventions.relationship_endpoints: source and target reference entity IDs

coverage_notes: BASIC is a family of dialects, not a single uniform implementation; syntax and behavior vary by dialect.
The user-provided reference grounds the historical overview and named dialects; extra technical connections are curated context.
The graph separates language features, standards, people, implementations, hardware, operating systems, and applications.

entities.name: BASIC
entities.description: Family of general-purpose high-level languages designed for ease of use and programming accessibility.

entities.name: John G. Kemeny
entities.description: Dartmouth mathematician and co-creator of BASIC; wrote the first version.

entities.name: Thomas E. Kurtz
entities.description: Dartmouth professor and co-creator who advocated programming literacy.

entities.name: John McCarthy
entities.description: Suggested time-sharing as a solution to the long delays of batch processing.

entities.name: David H. Ahl
entities.description: Promoted BASIC games, collected programs, and founded Creative Computing.

entities.name: Bill Gates
entities.description: Co-wrote Microsoft BASIC for the Altair 8800.

entities.name: Paul Allen
entities.description: Co-wrote Microsoft BASIC for the Altair 8800.

entities.name: Monte Davidoff
entities.description: Contributed to the Altair BASIC implementation, including floating-point routines.

entities.name: Edsger W. Dijkstra
entities.description: Known for a sharply critical 1975 statement about BASIC as a teaching language.

entities.name: Dartmouth College
entities.description: Institution where BASIC was developed.

entities.name: Dartmouth Time-Sharing System (DTSS)
entities.description: Interactive time-sharing environment that let multiple users edit and run BASIC programs concurrently.

entities.name: FORTRAN II
entities.description: Strong syntactic influence on early BASIC.

entities.name: ALGOL 60
entities.description: Language explored in earlier attempts to create accessible programming for students.

entities.name: JOSS
entities.description: Interactive language similar in spirit to BASIC and influential in the interactive-computing context.

entities.name: DARSIMCO
entities.description: Dartmouth Simplified Code, an earlier language experiment.

entities.name: DOPE
entities.description: Dartmouth Oversimplified Programming Experiment, an earlier teaching-language experiment.

entities.name: National Science Foundation
entities.description: Provided a $300,000 grant that funded computing equipment for the Dartmouth project.

entities.name: GE-225
entities.description: Computer purchased for the original BASIC project.

entities.name: Datanet-30
entities.description: Real-time processor handling terminal I/O.

entities.name: Teletype Model 33
entities.description: Teleprinter used to interact with the Dartmouth system.

entities.name: BASIC first release
entities.description: First BASIC version released on May 1, 1964.

entities.name: Dartmouth BASIC
entities.description: Original BASIC dialect developed for the Dartmouth time-sharing system.

entities.name: Time-sharing
entities.description: Allocates processing time among interactive users to provide responsive shared computing.

entities.name: Batch processing
entities.description: Runs submitted jobs with delayed feedback, helping motivate interactive BASIC.

entities.name: Minicomputers
entities.description: Mid-sized systems on which BASIC spread in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

entities.name: Microcomputers
entities.description: Small, affordable computers that made BASIC ubiquitous in personal computing.

entities.name: Home computer era
entities.description: Late 1970s and 1980s period when BASIC was commonly built into consumer computers.

entities.name: Programming literacy
entities.description: Goal of enabling students outside traditional STEM fields to use computers.

entities.name: Read-only memory (ROM)
entities.description: Non-volatile memory used to include BASIC interpreters in many home computers.

entities.name: Interpreter
entities.description: Executes or translates instructions incrementally; suited to memory-limited systems.

entities.name: Compiler
entities.description: Translates a program into a separate executable or lower-level representation.

entities.name: Structured programming
entities.description: Uses explicit control structures and procedures rather than relying on arbitrary jumps.

entities.name: Procedural programming
entities.description: Organizes programs into procedures or subroutines.

entities.name: Object-oriented programming
entities.description: Organizes software around objects containing data and behavior.

entities.name: Event-driven programming
entities.description: Runs handlers in response to events such as GUI actions.

entities.name: Rapid application development
entities.description: Uses visual design tools and quick iteration, associated with Visual Basic.

entities.name: Integrated development environment (IDE)
entities.description: Combines editing, execution, debugging, and help.

entities.name: Memory constraints
entities.description: Small RAM budgets shaped early interpreters and Tiny BASIC.

entities.name: Dialect fragmentation
entities.description: BASIC has many variants with differing syntax, types, graphics, and runtime behavior.

entities.name: Portability across dialects
entities.description: Programs may require changes between BASIC variants.

entities.name: Testing
entities.description: Unit, integration, and regression tests preserve behavior during maintenance and porting.

entities.name: Legacy modernization
entities.description: Porting, refactoring, testing, and documenting older BASIC programs.

entities.name: Security considerations
entities.description: Review of input, file access, external calls, and runtime assumptions in BASIC programs.

entities.name: ANSI X3.60-1978 Minimal BASIC
entities.description: Withdrawn ANSI standard for Minimal BASIC.

entities.name: ISO/IEC 6373:1984 Minimal BASIC
entities.description: Withdrawn ISO/IEC standard defining Minimal BASIC.

entities.name: ECMA-55 Minimal BASIC
entities.description: ECMA Minimal BASIC standard similar to ANSI X3.60-1978.

entities.name: ANSI X3.113-1987 Full BASIC
entities.description: ANSI standard for Full BASIC.

entities.name: ISO/IEC 10279 Full BASIC
entities.description: ISO/IEC Full BASIC standard, listed by the source as in force with a 2024 revision.

entities.name: ISO/IEC 10279 Amendment 1
entities.description: Amendment adding modules and single-character input enhancement.

entities.name: ECMA-116 BASIC
entities.description: Withdrawn ECMA BASIC standard similar to ANSI Full BASIC.

entities.name: LET
entities.description: Assigns an expression to a variable; often optional in later dialects.

entities.name: DATA
entities.description: Stores literal values for later sequential reading.

entities.name: READ
entities.description: Reads values from DATA and advances the internal data pointer.

entities.name: RESTORE
entities.description: Resets the DATA pointer, optionally to a selected location in some dialects.

entities.name: DIM
entities.description: Declares or allocates array dimensions.

entities.name: IF THEN ELSE
entities.description: Conditional execution; early dialects often used a line number after THEN.

entities.name: FOR TO STEP NEXT
entities.description: Count-controlled loop with index and optional step.

entities.name: WHILE WEND
entities.description: Pre-test loop repeated while a condition is true in dialects supporting it.

entities.name: REPEAT UNTIL
entities.description: Loop repeated until a condition becomes true in dialects supporting it.

entities.name: DO LOOP
entities.description: Flexible loop form with optional WHILE or UNTIL conditions in later dialects.

entities.name: GOTO
entities.description: Transfers execution to a numbered or labelled line.

entities.name: GOSUB RETURN
entities.description: Calls a line-oriented subroutine and returns to the following statement.

entities.name: ON GOTO / ON GOSUB
entities.description: Selects a branch or subroutine target based on an expression.

entities.name: DEF FN
entities.description: Defines a function, historically often a single expression with constrained names.

entities.name: LIST
entities.description: Displays the stored source code.

entities.name: PRINT
entities.description: Writes text and values to a screen or output device.

entities.name: INPUT
entities.description: Prompts for and reads values into variables.

entities.name: TAB
entities.description: Moves output to a specified column or position.

entities.name: SPC
entities.description: Outputs a requested number of spaces.

entities.name: REM
entities.description: Introduces a remark or comment.

entities.name: USR
entities.description: Calls a machine-language routine in some dialects.

entities.name: CALL
entities.description: Calls an external or machine-level routine in dialects supporting it.

entities.name: TRON / TROFF
entities.description: Turns execution-line tracing on or off.

entities.name: ASM
entities.description: Allows assembly code to be embedded in some compiled dialects.

entities.name: ABS
entities.description: Returns absolute value.

entities.name: ATN
entities.description: Returns arctangent, typically in radians.

entities.name: COS
entities.description: Returns cosine, typically with angles in radians.

entities.name: EXP
entities.description: Returns the exponential function.

entities.name: INT
entities.description: Returns an integer-valued result; exact negative-value behavior varies by dialect.

entities.name: LOG
entities.description: Returns the natural logarithm.

entities.name: RND
entities.description: Generates pseudo-random values; exact semantics vary by dialect.

entities.name: SIN
entities.description: Returns sine, typically with angles in radians.

entities.name: SQR
entities.description: Returns square root.

entities.name: TAN
entities.description: Returns tangent.

entities.name: String variables ($ suffix)
entities.description: Many microcomputer dialects use a trailing dollar sign to mark string variables.

entities.name: Numeric variables
entities.description: Variables may use integer or floating-point representations.

entities.name: Integer
entities.description: Whole-number type or representation.

entities.name: Floating-point
entities.description: Approximate real-number representation.

entities.name: String
entities.description: Text values often delimited by double quotation marks.

entities.name: Array
entities.description: Indexed collection declared using DIM; indexing rules vary.

entities.name: Matrix operations
entities.description: Dartmouth BASIC included MAT operations; many microcomputer versions did not.

entities.name: Line numbers
entities.description: Early BASIC programs used numeric line labels for editing and branch targets.

entities.name: Labels
entities.description: Later dialects often use labels and procedures instead of mandatory line numbers.

entities.name: Colon statement separator
entities.description: Many dialects allow multiple statements on one line separated by a colon.

entities.name: Case insensitivity
entities.description: Many BASIC dialects treat keywords and identifiers case-insensitively.

entities.name: Implicit typing
entities.description: Some dialects infer types from suffixes or default rules.

entities.name: Local variables
entities.description: Structured dialects can scope variables within procedures.

entities.name: Parameterized procedures
entities.description: Later dialects allow subroutines and functions to accept arguments.

entities.name: Modules
entities.description: Some dialects support module-based program organization.

entities.name: Classes and objects
entities.description: Object-oriented dialects add types that bundle state and behavior.

entities.name: Events
entities.description: GUI-oriented dialects provide event handlers.

entities.name: File I/O
entities.description: Later dialects commonly support file opening, reading, writing, and closing.

entities.name: Graphics commands
entities.description: Many home-computer and game dialects add drawing, screen, sprite, and sound APIs.

entities.name: String manipulation
entities.description: Common functions provide length, substring, search, and concatenation.

entities.name: Direct mode
entities.description: Interactive mode where statements can be executed immediately at the prompt.

entities.name: Program mode
entities.description: Mode in which stored source lines are run as a program.

entities.name: Matrix arithmetic
entities.description: Matrix addition, multiplication, determinants, and related numerical operations.

entities.name: Input validation
entities.description: Checking user-supplied values for validity and expected ranges.

entities.name: File system access
entities.description: Facilities for reading and writing files in later BASIC dialects.

entities.name: Runtime library
entities.description: Runtime-provided built-ins, I/O, string handling, graphics, and system services.

entities.name: External libraries

entities.name: Game loop
entities.description: Repeated input, update, and rendering cycle implementable with BASIC loops and graphics APIs.

entities.name: Event loop
entities.description: Dispatches callbacks in response to user or system events.
